examples.trans: Your dad gave it to us as a gift.

examples.text: Подарили колбасу, так будь благодарен!
examples.trans: They gifted you sausage, so be grateful!

meanings.en: actually, strictly speaking, as a matter of fact
meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще-то'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Вообще-то это наш блендер.
examples.trans: Actually, that is our blender.

examples.text: А вообще-то я ещё не решил.
examples.trans: Actually, I haven't decided yet.

examples.text: Вообще-то это моё место.
examples.trans: Actually, this is my seat.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Дима, завязывай этот балаган.
examples.trans: Dima, wrap up this circus.

examples.text: А где у вас тут это в сценарии?
examples.trans: And where do you have that in the script?

examples.text: Это я импровизирую.
examples.trans: That is me improvising.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вообще-то это наш блендер.
examples.trans: Actually, that is our blender.

examples.text: Зато у нашего сына своя комната.
examples.trans: On the other hand, our son has his own room.

examples.text: Это же наш дом, и на стол здесь накрывать будем мы.
examples.trans: After all, this is our home, and we will set the table here.
